messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: prod canary rollout v3.1.2 — latency spike + throughput drop detected. kernel_fallback rate high. Paging oncall.
sara (eng-oncall): on it, joining metrics.
jc (eng-runtime): confirm — canary pool (canary-rt-03) latency p95 ~2.1s (baseline 350ms), throughput down ~35%. kernel_selector switching to fallback kernels mid-request.
mike (sre): rolling back canary weight now. moving traffic 50% -> 10%. executing rollout revert.
alex (prod): customer impact? support seeing errors?
emily (support): two orgs reporting timeouts on embeddings endpoint. tickets: #SEV1-7789, #SEV2-7790. tagging account IDs.
jc (eng-runtime): logs show batching windows collapsing, too many small micro-batches -> kernel fallback thrash. snippet from node:
```
[WARN] kernel_selector: fallback chosen for model-x @ step=42
batch_window_ms=5 -> 1
prefetch_evictions=high
```
sara (eng-oncall): can we flip the feature flag kill-switch? LaunchDarkly flag `enable_canary_fastpath` -> false?
mike (sre): doing LD toggle now: `ldctl toggle enable_canary_fastpath --env prod --off` — applied.
jc (eng-runtime): confirmed flag flip reached canary nodes. starting forced kernel affinity to stable kernel: `rtctl kernel-affinity set model-x stable-avx --targets canary-rt-*`
alex (prod): traffic now at 10%, flag off, kernels pinned. monitoring.
emily (support): customers reporting partial improvement but still intermittent 504s for large batched requests.
jc (eng-runtime): I think micro-batching policy adaptive timer is causing rapid window shrink when load fluctuations hit. mitigation: disable adaptive micro-batch on canary: `servicectl set-param microbatch.adaptive false --env prod --scope canary`.
mike (sre): applied microbatch adaptive=false on canary. also increased batch window to 20ms to stabilize.
sara (eng-oncall): metrics streaming — latency p95 falling to 420ms, throughput recovering to ~92% of baseline.
emily (support): updated tickets: customers notified, workaround suggested (smaller request sizes). no new SEV1 reports.
jc (eng-runtime): request we hold rollout until next deploy window. recommend full revert of v3.1.2 from rollout pipeline.
alex (prod): agreed — cancel remainder of rollout, revert artifact to v3.1.1. initiating revert pipeline.
mike (sre): revert started: `redwoodctl rollout revert --to v3.1.1 --env prod --force` — ETA ~3m.
sara (eng-oncall): notify infra teams if any node restarts occur during revert.
jc (eng-runtime): quick postmortem notes: root causes = aggressive micro-batching adaptive policy + kernel selector heuristics that reacted poorly to collapsing batch sizes; combined with new kernel selection fallback path in v3.1.2.
emily (support): created customer status update draft, will send once stable window confirmed.
mike (sre): revert finished. all canary nodes now serving v3.1.1. final checks: p95=360ms, throughput ~100%.
sara (eng-oncall): service stable. moving to 1:1 handoff to rachel for monitoring through next hour.
rachel (eng-oncall-2): ack — taking handoff. I'll keep watch on canary and escalate if any regression.
jc (eng-runtime): followups: add tighter e2e canary tests for batching patterns, add guard in kernel_selector to avoid fallback churn under high eviction rates, and add canary metric alert for kernel_fallback_rate > 5%.
alex (prod): will schedule a postmortem and customer comms review. thanks everyone.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: rolling revert complete, customer impact contained. incident closed to oncall; postmortem to be filed.
